source_refs.note: Book p. 35-36: derivative of sin x by definition, Try yourself! box, derivatives of the other trigonometric functions, Example 1, box of six trigonometric derivatives, Example 2

blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Ab tak aap ne polynomials aur rational functions ke derivatives nikale hain. Aaj hum trigonometric functions (sin, cos, tan waghera) ke derivatives nikalenge. Yeh functions har us cheez mein aate hain jo ghoomti hai ya baar baar dohraati hai: pendulum, lehrein (waves), AC bijli. Hum pehle sin x ka derivative seedha definition se saabit karenge, phir baqi functions ke derivatives rules se aasani se nikal aayenge.

Kitab pehle ek shart lagati hai: trigonometric functions ke derivatives nikalte waqt angle radians mein naapa jata hai. Ab \(f(x) = \sin x\) ka derivative nikalte hain.
Yahan \(f(x + h) = \sin(x + h)\) hai, aur
\[f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}\]
(derivative ki definition se)
\[= \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\sin(x+h) - \sin x}{h}\]
(values rakh kar)
Ab formula \(\sin p - \sin q = 2\cos\frac{p+q}{2}\sin\frac{p-q}{2}\) lagate hain, jahan \(p = x + h\) aur \(q = x\):
\[\dfrac{p+q}{2} = \dfrac{x+h+x}{2} = \dfrac{2x+h}{2}\]
\[\dfrac{p-q}{2} = \dfrac{x+h-x}{2} = \dfrac{h}{2}\]
\[f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{2\cos\left(\frac{2x+h}{2}\right)\sin\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)}{h}\]
Ab limit \(h \to 0\) lagate hain:
\[= \lim_{h \to 0}\cos\left(\dfrac{2x+h}{2}\right)\]
\[\quad \cdot \lim_{h \to 0}\dfrac{\sin(h/2)}{h/2}\]
\[= \cos x\,(1) = \cos x\]
\(\left(\because \lim_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} = 1,\ \theta \text{ radians mein}\right)\)
Is tarah \(\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \cos x\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Har line mein kya hua, yeh samajhna zaroori hai, ratta nahin:
1. Pehle definition likhi aur f ki jagah sin rakha.
2. Do sines ka farq (\(\sin p - \sin q\)) ek product mein badla. Yeh is liye kiya ke ek factor \(\sin(h/2)\) saamne aa jaye, jis ki limit hum jaante hain.
3. \(\frac{2\sin(h/2)}{h} = \frac{\sin(h/2)}{h/2}\). Aage wala 2 neeche ja kar \(h\) ko \(h/2\) bana deta hai. Ab \(\theta = h/2\) rakh kar standard limit \(\lim_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} = 1\) lag jati hai.
4. \(h \to 0\) par \(\cos\left(\frac{2x+h}{2}\right) \to \cos x\). Is tarah jawab \(\cos x\) aaya.
Radians kyun? Kyun ke \(\lim_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} = 1\) sirf radians mein sach hai. Degrees mein yeh limit \(\frac{\pi}{180}\) hoti, aur har trigonometric derivative ke saath yeh faltu factor chipka rehta. Is liye calculus mein hamesha radians.

blocks.title: The derivative of the sine function is the cosine function
Try yourself!
blocks.text: Definition se saabit kijiye: \(\frac{d}{dx}(\cos x) = -\sin x\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Try yourself! ke liye rehnumai (bilkul sine wale qadam, bas formula alag hai):
Formula \(\cos p - \cos q = -2\sin\frac{p+q}{2}\sin\frac{p-q}{2}\) lagayein, jahan \(p = x + h\), \(q = x\):
\[\dfrac{\cos(x+h) - \cos x}{h}\]
\[= \dfrac{-2\sin\left(\frac{2x+h}{2}\right)\sin\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)}{h}\]
\[= -\sin\left(\dfrac{2x+h}{2}\right) \cdot \dfrac{\sin(h/2)}{h/2}\]
Ab \(h \to 0\): pehla factor \(\sin x\) ki taraf aur doosra 1 ki taraf jata hai, is liye
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\cos x) = -\sin x\]
Dhyan dein: cos ke formula mein shuru mein minus hai, isi liye jawab mein minus aata hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(x = 0\) par \(\sin x\) ka graph kitni tezi se barh raha hai? Formula kehta hai slope \(\cos 0 = 1\). Aur \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) par, jahan sine apni sab se oonchi value 1 par hai, slope \(\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0\) hai. Kya yeh graph ki shakal se mel khata hai? (Haan: choti par graph ek lamhe ke liye seedha ho jata hai.)
Derivative of the Other Trigonometric Functions

Kitab kehti hai: \(\sin x\) aur \(\cos x\) ke derivatives definition se nikalne ke baad, baqi trigonometric functions ke derivatives product rule aur quotient rule se nikal sakte hain. Wajah yeh hai ke baqi chaaron functions sin aur cos se hi bante hain: \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\), \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\), \(\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}\), \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\).

blocks.title: Example 1
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = \tan x\).
Maloom karna: \(f'(x)\).
Tareeqa: \(\tan x\) ko \(\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\) likhenge aur quotient rule lagayenge. \(\sin x\) aur \(\cos x\) ke derivatives hum definition se pehle hi nikal chuke hain, wohi yahan kaam aayenge. Seedha limit wali definition lagana bhi mumkin hai, magar quotient rule se kaam bohat chhota ho jata hai.

Step 1: tan x ko quotient ki shakal mein likhein
\[f(x) = \tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\]
Kyun: \(\tan x\) ka derivative abhi humein maloom nahin, lekin \(\sin x\) aur \(\cos x\) ke maloom hain. Quotient rule inhein jor deta hai: \(u = \sin x\) (upar), \(v = \cos x\) (neeche).

Step 2: Quotient rule lagayein (x ke lihaaz se differentiate)
\[u'v = (\sin x)'\cos x = \cos x\cos x\]
\[uv' = \sin x(\cos x)' = \sin x(-\sin x)\]
\[f'(x) = \dfrac{\cos x\cos x - \sin x(-\sin x)}{\cos^{2} x}\]
Kyun: \((\sin x)' = \cos x\) aur \((\cos x)' = -\sin x\). Formula hai \(\frac{u'v - uv'}{v^{2}}\).
Dhyan dein: \(uv'\) mein pehle se minus hai, aur formula mein bhi minus hai; dono mil kar plus banenge.

Step 3: Simplify karein
\[f'(x) = \dfrac{\cos^{2} x + \sin^{2} x}{\cos^{2} x}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\cos^{2} x} = \sec^{2} x\]
Kyun: minus guna minus plus hota hai; identity \(\sin^{2} x + \cos^{2} x = 1\) lagi; aur \(\frac{1}{\cos x} = \sec x\) hai, is liye \(\frac{1}{\cos^{2} x} = \sec^{2} x\).

Tasdeeq: \(x = \frac{\pi}{4}\) par formula \(\sec^{2}\frac{\pi}{4} = 2\) deta hai. Calculator se \(\frac{\tan(0.7864) - \tan(0.7844)}{0.002} \approx 2.000\) aata hai. Dono slopes barabar hain, yani jawab sahi hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab Example 1 ke saath "(By using definition)" likhti hai, lekin hal (solution) mein limit wali definition seedhi istemal nahin hui. Asal mein quotient rule laga hai, aur saath \((\sin x)' = \cos x\), \((\cos x)' = -\sin x\) use hue hain (jo khud definition se nikle thay). Sahi label '(By using the quotient rule)' hona chahiye. Jawab \(\frac{d}{dx}(\tan x) = \sec^{2} x\) bilkul sahi hai.

blocks.title: The Derivatives of Six Trigonometric Functions
blocks.text:
(i) \(\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x) = \cos x\)
(ii) \(\frac{d}{dx}(\cos x) = -\sin x\)
(iii) \(\frac{d}{dx}(\tan x) = \sec^{2} x\)
(iv) \(\frac{d}{dx}(\cot x) = -\csc^{2} x\)
(v) \(\frac{d}{dx}(\sec x) = \sec x\tan x\)
(vi) \(\frac{d}{dx}(\csc x) = -\csc x\cot x\)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Kitab ke box mein formula (vi) \(\frac{d}{dx}(\csc x) = \csc x\cot x\) chhapa hai, yani minus ka sign ghaib hai. Sahi formula yeh hai:
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\csc x) = -\csc x\cot x\]
Saboot: \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\). Quotient rule se \((\csc x)' = \frac{0 \cdot \sin x - 1 \cdot \cos x}{\sin^{2} x} = -\frac{1}{\sin x}\cdot\frac{\cos x}{\sin x} = -\csc x\cot x\). Kitab khud Example 2 mein minus wala sahi formula use karti hai. Upar box mein humne sahi formula likha hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Baqi teen formulas bhi quotient rule se isi tarah nikalte hain. Khud kar ke dekhiye, yeh exam mein aksar aata hai:
\(\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}\): \((\sec x)' = \frac{0 - 1(-\sin x)}{\cos^{2} x} = \frac{1}{\cos x}\cdot\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \sec x\tan x\).
\(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\): \((\cot x)' = \frac{-\sin^{2} x - \cos^{2} x}{\sin^{2} x} = -\frac{1}{\sin^{2} x} = -\csc^{2} x\).
Yaad karne ka aasan tareeqa: jin functions ke naam 'co' se shuru hote hain (\(\cos\), \(\cot\), \(\csc\)), un sab ke derivatives mein minus hota hai. Aur jodiyan bana lijiye: \(\tan \to \sec^{2}\) ki jodi \(\cot \to -\csc^{2}\) hai; \(\sec \to \sec\tan\) ki jodi \(\csc \to -\csc\cot\) hai. Har jagah function ko us ke co-function se badlo aur minus laga do.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps:
Diya gaya: \(y = x^{2}\csc x\).
Maloom karna: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
Tareeqa: yahan do functions zarb ho rahe hain, \(u = x^{2}\) aur \(v = \csc x\). Zarb dekhte hi product rule yaad aana chahiye. Saath \((\csc x)' = -\csc x\cot x\) chahiye hoga (minus ke saath).

Step 1: Product rule (x ke lihaaz se differentiate)
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (x^{2})'\csc x + x^{2}(\csc x)'\]
Kyun: \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\): pehle ka derivative guna doosra, jama pehla guna doosre ka derivative.

Step 2: Derivatives rakhein
\[= 2x\csc x + x^{2}(-\csc x\cot x)\]
\[= 2x\csc x - x^{2}\csc x\cot x\]
Kyun: power rule se \((x^{2})' = 2x\), aur formula (vi) se \((\csc x)' = -\csc x\cot x\).
Dhyan dein: yahan minus ka sign bohat aham hai; isi se pata chalta hai ke kitab ke box mein (vi) ka sign ghalat chhapa hai.

Step 3: Common factor bahar nikalein
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x\csc x\,(2 - x\cot x)\]
Kyun: dono terms mein \(x\csc x\) mojood hai, is liye jawab ko chhota aur saaf karne ke liye bahar nikal liya.
Tasdeeq: bracket khol kar dekhein: \(x\csc x \cdot 2 - x\csc x \cdot x\cot x = 2x\csc x - x^{2}\csc x\cot x\), jo bilkul Step 2 wali line hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(a) \(\frac{d}{dx}(x\sin x) = (1)\sin x + x\cos x = \sin x + x\cos x\). Yahan \(x\) aur \(\sin x\) zarb hain, is liye product rule laga.
(b) \(\frac{d}{dx}(3\tan x - 2\sec x) = 3\sec^{2} x - 2\sec x\tan x\). Yahan constant multiple aur difference rule lage: numbers apni jagah rahe aur har term ka alag derivative liya.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(\frac{d}{dx}(\sin x\cos x)\) kya hoga? Product rule se \(\cos^{2} x - \sin^{2} x\) aata hai, jo \(\cos 2x\) hai. Ab \(\sin x\cos x = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2x\) likh kar sochiye ke kya yeh jawab theek lagta hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Angle hamesha radians mein; sin x ka derivative definition se \(\lim_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} = 1\) par khara hai.
2. \((\sin x)' = \cos x\), \((\cos x)' = -\sin x\); baqi chaar quotient rule se nikalte hain.
3. \((\tan x)' = \sec^{2} x\), \((\cot x)' = -\csc^{2} x\), \((\sec x)' = \sec x\tan x\), \((\csc x)' = -\csc x\cot x\).
4. "Co" wale functions (cos, cot, csc) ke derivatives mein minus hota hai.
5. Kitab ke box mein (vi) ka minus chhutt gaya hai; sahi \(-\csc x\cot x\) hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \((\cos x)' = \sin x\) ya \((\csc x)' = \csc x\cot x\) likh dena: minus bhool gaye.
2. Degrees mein kaam karna: yeh formulas sirf radians mein sahi hain.
3. \((\tan x)' = \sec x\) likh dena: sahi \(\sec^{2} x\) hai, square zaroori hai.
4. Product mein seedha dono derivatives zarb kar dena, jaise \((x^{2}\csc x)' = 2x(-\csc x\cot x)\): yeh ghalat hai, product rule lagta hai.
